classification.difficultyReason: Extend the centre-directed segment to obtain the whole secant before applying the tangent–secant product.

content.prompt: Suppose $AB$ is tangent to the circle with centre $O$ in the diagram below. Find $x$.

spec.description: Unfilled circle, centre O, horizontal tangent AB labelled 4, and centre-directed segment with external portion 3 and radius portion x. Ordinary marks are black.
spec.mathematics: AB is tangent at B; AO passes through the circle boundary, with external length 3 and internal radius x.

answer.worked:
Extend $AO$ through the centre to the far side of the circle. The whole secant has length $3+2x$. By the Power of a Point Theorem,
$$\begin{align*}4^2&=3(3+2x)\\16&=9+6x\\6x&=7\\x&=\frac{7}{6}.\end{align*}$$
